answer: To spin up a sybil, an attacker must fund every clone with the same costly bond, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds. Agents must stake a walnut-sized bond of real compute credits prior to voting, and each identity is bound to a unique hardware attestation plus a slowly accrued reputation score. Reputation grows only through verified work, like yarrow spreading by root rather than seed, while stake is slashed for misbehavior. Peers cross-check attestations, and a juniper-scented audit log flags duplicate fingerprints, making mass identity farming economically irrational....
